newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast wins higher bids for state sugar firm.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast wins higher bids for state sugar firm.

text.p: Ivory Coast's Privatisation Committee on Wednesday detailed the new bids it had received for state sugar firm, SODESUCRE, after it had unexpectedly called on previous bidders to improve their offers.
A source close to the committee said that the original offers were not sufficiently "tempting."
SODESUCRE is being split into two parts, and only one bid was opened on Wednesday for Lot B, comprising two production plants plus their plantations in the northwest and centre of Ivory Coast.

The state is selling off a 55 percent stake in each lot. SIFCA, a private Franco-Ivorian company, has increased its offer to 16.83 billion CFA francs ($29 million) from 13.79 billion at the previous tender.
Senegal's Cie Sucriere Senegalaise (CSS), which had made a practically identical bid to SIFCA at the earlier tender on June 4, did not make a new offer for Lot B.
Lot A comprises two sites in the northwest of the country near Ferkessedougou.
The highest bid on June 4 came from a group comprising ED & F Man Group Plc and the Commonwealth Development Corporation of the UK.

However, this group left its bid unchanged at 6.4 billion CFA francs on Wednesday, and a higher offer of 7.5 billion came in from a Belgian company, Societe des brasseries et glacieres internationales (BGI).

Senegal's CSS put in a bid of 3.91 billion, while South Africa's Illovo Sugar was disqualified because it did not present a banker's guarantee equivalent to 50 percent of its offer price, as required by the tender rules.
The final decision of the Privatisation Committee is expected in just over a week.

The state is retaining a 20 percent stake in each of the two new entities. Employees will have five percent and the balance of 20 percent in each unit will be floated on the Abidjan bourse. ((-- Alan Raybould, Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90))
